$comment: The variation catalog. scripts/direction.mjs draws one entry from each list to fix a unique look for a reel, and injects the result into the Gemini brief and the asset prompts. Add entries freely — the picker reads whatever is here. Every artDirection.backdrop must name a variant that exists in src/components/Backdrop.tsx, and every typeSystem.primary must name a component exported from src/components/KineticType.tsx or Type.tsx.

artDirections.name: Paper collage documentary
artDirections.summary: Torn-edge magazine collage on warm paper. Scissor-cut photography, halftone dots, hand-drawn marker emphasis. The Vox / Johnny Harris house look.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Heavy sentence-case grotesk, tight tracking, marker highlight and hand-drawn underline as the emphasis language.
artDirections.imageDirection: Editorial magazine collage cutout with a crisp 12px white paper border as if scissor-cut from a printed page. Slightly desaturated documentary photography, cool neutral grade, soft even light, gentle film grain.
artDirections.propDirection: Real physical objects photographed flat on a desk, slight drop shadow, as if pasted into a scrapbook.

artDirections.name: Risograph zine print
artDirections.summary: Two-ink risograph printing — heavy grain, visible misregistration, flat spot colours knocking out of each other. Everything looks printed rather than rendered.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Chunky display type that overprints the artwork, with a 3px offset ghost in the second ink colour.
artDirections.imageDirection: High-contrast two-tone risograph print of the subject, coarse visible grain and halftone dither, flat posterised shadows, slight ink misregistration, printed on uncoated paper.
artDirections.propDirection: Objects reduced to two flat ink layers with visible dot texture and a misregistered outline.
artDirections.avoid: Photographic gradients, soft shadows, realistic depth of field.

artDirections.name: Swiss editorial grid
artDirections.summary: International-style poster discipline. A visible modular grid, enormous type set to the baseline, generous white space, a single accent colour doing all the work.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Left-aligned, flush-left ragged-right, very large weights against very small labels. Rules and hairlines instead of decoration.
artDirections.imageDirection: Clean studio photograph of the subject, even diffuse light, neutral grade, no props beyond what the subject holds, composed with generous negative space.
artDirections.propDirection: One object, centred, shot straight on under flat studio light, no styling.
artDirections.avoid: Texture overlays, hand-drawn marks, centred symmetry everywhere.

artDirections.name: Night data room
artDirections.summary: Dark operations-room look. Glowing data lines over near-black, numbers as the hero, light spilling from the graphics onto everything else.
artDirections.typographyFeel: White and accent type on near-black, tabular numerals oversized, thin dividing rules, a faint glow behind the emphasis word.
artDirections.imageDirection: Low-key photograph of the subject lit from one side by cool screen light in a dark room, deep shadows, the face and hands catching the light.
artDirections.propDirection: Object lit by a single cool rim light against darkness, subtle specular highlights.
artDirections.avoid: Paper texture, warm beige, anything that reads as printed.

artDirections.name: Blueprint schematic
artDirections.summary: Everything drawn as a technical schematic — measurement ticks, callout leader lines, exploded diagrams, annotations in a monospaced hand.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Sentence-case display type paired with small monospaced annotation labels and dimension arrows.
artDirections.imageDirection: Photograph of the subject shot flat and square to the camera, even light, so it can be annotated with callout lines. Neutral cool grade.
artDirections.propDirection: Object photographed dead-on from a single axis like a parts catalogue plate.
artDirections.avoid: Soft romantic lighting, collage edges, confetti.

artDirections.name: Archive broadcast
artDirections.summary: Degraded tape footage — scanlines, slight chroma bleed, a lower-third that slides in like a 1990s news bug. Used to make the old way feel genuinely old.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Condensed news-bug lower thirds and timecode-style labels next to modern sentence-case headlines.
artDirections.imageDirection: Slightly degraded archival video still of the subject, softened detail, mild chroma bleed, faint scanlines, colour shifted slightly warm.
artDirections.propDirection: Object shot as a 1990s catalogue photograph, slightly soft, mild colour cast.

artDirections.name: Gallery minimal
artDirections.summary: One idea per frame, hung like a gallery print. Huge margins, a soft floor shadow, and long quiet holds that let the narration carry.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Small confident type in a lot of space. Emphasis comes from scale and position, not from marks.
artDirections.imageDirection: Museum-quality photograph of the subject, soft directional light, matte finish, restrained natural colour, composed centrally with air around it.
artDirections.propDirection: Single object on a plain surface with a soft long shadow, like a product plate.
artDirections.avoid: Busy overlays, more than two elements on screen at once.

artDirections.name: Chalk lecture
artDirections.summary: Ideas drawn as they are spoken, on a dark green board. Arrows, circles and underlines appear by hand; nothing is pre-drawn.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Chalky white and pastel type with hand-drawn circles and arrows, deliberately slightly irregular.
artDirections.imageDirection: Photograph of the subject with a soft warm classroom light, natural expression, mid-shot, so it can sit beside drawn annotation.
artDirections.propDirection: Object photographed simply so it can be circled and annotated with chalk marks.
artDirections.avoid: Photographic gradients behind the board, glossy UI panels.

artDirections.name: Neon gradient
artDirections.summary: Saturated brand-gradient fields, soft volumetric glow, floating glass panels. Confident and modern, the look of a launch film.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Gradient-filled display type with a soft bloom, set against translucent frosted panels.
artDirections.imageDirection: Photograph of the subject lit with coloured gradient light from two sides, glossy modern grade, crisp detail, shallow depth of field.
artDirections.propDirection: Object on a reflective surface lit with coloured gradient light and a soft bloom.
artDirections.avoid: Paper grain, halftone dots, hand-drawn marks.

artDirections.name: Newsprint tabloid
artDirections.summary: Cheap newsprint, ragged column rules, a banner headline that takes the whole frame. Loud, urgent and a little bit shouty — in the layout, not the words.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Banner headline across the full width with a rule under it, body set in narrow columns, kicker in a black bar.
artDirections.imageDirection: Coarse newsprint halftone photograph of the subject, visible dot screen, high contrast black and white with one spot colour.
artDirections.propDirection: Object as a newsprint halftone cut, hard black dots, slightly off-register spot colour.

artDirections.name: Clean product film
artDirections.summary: The product's own interface is the star. Crisp white set, floating UI panels with real shadows, everything shot like a keynote.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Calm sentence-case type, plenty of leading, colour used only on the one word that matters.
artDirections.imageDirection: Bright clean photograph of the subject on a seamless white set, soft even light, crisp modern grade, gentle contact shadow.
artDirections.propDirection: Object on seamless white with a soft contact shadow, keynote product-shot lighting.

artDirections.name: Duotone split
artDirections.summary: The frame is always divided — old world against new, cost against saving. Each half gets its own duotone treatment and they fight for space.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Type crosses the divide, one half in each colour, so the split reads before the words do.
artDirections.imageDirection: Duotone photograph of the subject, two-colour gradient map, strong contrast, no midtone colour.
artDirections.propDirection: Object duotoned in the same two colours, silhouette-clear.

artDirections.name: Sticker scrapbook
artDirections.summary: Taped, stickered and annotated. Washi tape corners, circled notes in the margin, elements slightly rotated as if stuck down by hand.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Type on taped-down cards at small rotations, handwritten-feeling annotations pointing at things.
artDirections.imageDirection: Polaroid-style photograph of the subject with a warm flash-lit look, slight vignette, as if pinned to a board.
artDirections.propDirection: Object photographed as if lying on a desk and about to be taped down, soft top light.

artDirections.name: Terminal mono
artDirections.summary: A monospaced world. Text types itself, numbers tick in fixed columns, a cursor blinks. Reads as the machine doing the work.
artDirections.typographyFeel: Monospaced labels and counters against one large proportional headline, so the contrast between machine and human voice is visible.
artDirections.imageDirection: Photograph of the subject lit by monitor light in a quiet room, cool grade, sharp detail, restrained composition.
artDirections.propDirection: Object on a dark desk surface under a single cool overhead light.

typeSystems.name: Word punch
typeSystems.how: Words punch in one at a time with a spring overshoot, each pinned to the frame it is spoken.

typeSystems.name: Mask rise
typeSystems.how: Each line rises out from behind a hard mask edge, like type pushed up through a slot.

typeSystems.name: Typewriter
typeSystems.how: Characters type in with a blinking caret, at a rate matched to the narration.

typeSystems.name: Character cascade
typeSystems.how: Every character enters on its own stagger with a small rotation, so the line assembles like falling tiles.

typeSystems.name: Vertical roll
typeSystems.how: Words roll up out of a clipped window, the previous word rolling out of the top.

typeSystems.name: Blur to focus
typeSystems.how: Type resolves from heavy blur into sharpness, like a lens finding focus.

typeSystems.name: Karaoke fill
typeSystems.how: The whole line is present in a dimmed colour and fills with the accent colour exactly as each word is spoken.

typeSystems.name: Word swap
typeSystems.how: A fixed sentence with one slot, and the word in that slot is replaced two or three times.

typeSystems.name: Split flap
typeSystems.how: Letters flip through like an airport departures board before settling.

typeSystems.name: Elastic slam
typeSystems.how: Type slams in oversized and settles with an elastic overshoot and a frame shake.

typeSystems.name: Scramble settle
typeSystems.how: Characters cycle through random glyphs and resolve left to right into the real word.

typeSystems.name: Stacked slam
typeSystems.how: Lines land one under another, each one knocking the stack slightly, building a block of type.

editLanguages.name: Whip cut
editLanguages.how: Hard whip pans link scenes. Motion leaves frame one way and enters the next the same way, so the cut feels like a head turn.

editLanguages.name: Beat-locked triple
editLanguages.how: Three rapid cuts land on three consecutive stressed words, then the edit holds. The burst is the punctuation.
editLanguages.pace: bursts of 8–12 frames inside slower scenes

editLanguages.name: Match cut
editLanguages.how: Each cut matches a shape or a position across the boundary — a circle becomes a clock, a rectangle becomes a screen.

editLanguages.name: Freeze and annotate
editLanguages.how: Motion stops dead on a key word and annotations draw onto the frozen frame before movement resumes.

editLanguages.name: Zoom punch
editLanguages.how: Every emphasis word is a hard scale step into the frame, never a smooth zoom. The punch is on the consonant.

editLanguages.name: Long take drift
editLanguages.how: Very few cuts. The camera drifts slowly across a wide collage and elements animate in place as they are named.

editLanguages.name: Jump stutter
editLanguages.how: Small jump cuts inside the same composition, elements repositioning between frames, building nervous energy.

editLanguages.name: Speed ramp
editLanguages.how: Motion accelerates through the dull part and slams to a stop on the point being made.

editLanguages.name: Split screen
editLanguages.how: Two states run side by side and the divider moves to award space to whichever side the narration favours.

editLanguages.name: L-cut lead
editLanguages.how: The next scene's sound and first graphic arrive before the picture cuts, so each scene pulls the last one forward.

motionMotifs.name: Dot matrix units
motionMotifs.how: A grid of dots where a counted number fills in — hours, patients, forms. Abstract quantity made countable.

motionMotifs.name: Timeline rail
motionMotifs.how: A horizontal rail with markers that fill in as the narration walks through a sequence.

motionMotifs.name: Path trace
motionMotifs.how: A line draws itself between points with a travelling dot, showing a journey or a flow.

motionMotifs.name: Orbit system
motionMotifs.how: Satellites orbit a centre — the product at the middle, the things it touches circling it.

motionMotifs.name: Stacked cards
motionMotifs.how: A parallax stack of cards that fans out and recollapses, for a set of things becoming one thing.

motionMotifs.name: Split compare
motionMotifs.how: A moving divider between two states, the wipe itself carrying the argument.

motionMotifs.name: Pulse map
motionMotifs.how: A field of nodes with pings travelling between them — reach, network, adoption.

motionMotifs.name: Radial burst
motionMotifs.how: Speed lines firing out from the emphasis word on the stressed syllable.

motionMotifs.name: Halftone wave
motionMotifs.how: A field of dots swelling in a wave, for ambient listening, signal or breathing.

motionMotifs.name: Progress arc
motionMotifs.how: A circular gauge filling to a number, for time saved, completion, coverage.

motionMotifs.name: Isometric grid
motionMotifs.how: Isometric tiles rising out of a plane in sequence — building, scaling, stacking up.

motionMotifs.name: Film strip
motionMotifs.how: A strip of frames scrolling past, each one a moment in the story.

cameraLanguages.name: Locked off
cameraLanguages.how: The frame never moves. Everything inside it does. Stillness makes the motion inside read louder.

cameraLanguages.name: Slow push in
cameraLanguages.how: A continuous 3–6% scale push across each scene, so the frame is always closing in.

cameraLanguages.name: Handheld drift
cameraLanguages.how: A small noise-driven wander of a few pixels, enough to feel operated rather than rendered.

cameraLanguages.name: Whip pan links
cameraLanguages.how: The frame whips sideways between compositions inside a scene, not just between scenes.

cameraLanguages.name: Parallax layers
cameraLanguages.how: Background, mid and foreground move at different rates, giving real depth to a flat collage.

cameraLanguages.name: Overhead tabletop
cameraLanguages.how: Shot from directly above a surface, with hands and objects entering from the frame edges.

cameraLanguages.name: Rack focus
cameraLanguages.how: Blur transfers between a foreground and a background element as attention moves.

cameraLanguages.name: Side dolly
cameraLanguages.how: The frame tracks sideways across a wide scene, revealing the next element rather than cutting to it.

narrativeArcs.name: Cost then cure
narrativeArcs.shape: Make the viewer feel what today costs them, introduce the product once the cost is felt, prove one mechanism, close on the reclaimed version of the opening.

narrativeArcs.name: Myth bust
narrativeArcs.shape: State the thing everyone believes, show why it is wrong with a concrete example, replace it with what is actually true, close on what that means for the viewer.

narrativeArcs.name: Day in the life
narrativeArcs.shape: Walk one real person through a single day, hour by hour, and let the product appear at the point the day would normally break.

narrativeArcs.name: Before / after mirror
narrativeArcs.shape: Two halves that rhyme shot for shot — the same moments, once without and once with. The rhyme is the argument.

narrativeArcs.name: Countdown list
narrativeArcs.shape: Three things, counted down, each one a self-contained beat with its own visual device, converging on one conclusion.

narrativeArcs.name: Origin story
narrativeArcs.shape: Open on the specific moment the problem was noticed, follow what was tried, land on what was built and why it is shaped the way it is.

narrativeArcs.name: Objection handling
narrativeArcs.shape: Name the viewer's real objection out loud in the first five seconds, take it seriously, then dismantle it with one piece of evidence.

narrativeArcs.name: Question hook
narrativeArcs.shape: Ask a question the viewer cannot answer, withhold the answer while building the stakes, pay it off in the last third.

narrativeArcs.name: Numbers ladder
narrativeArcs.shape: Climb a ladder of numbers, each one bigger or smaller than the last, until the scale of the thing is undeniable, then name the cause.

narrativeArcs.name: Contrarian take
narrativeArcs.shape: Argue against the obvious solution everyone reaches for, show its hidden cost, then offer the unobvious one.

openingGambits.how: Open on a single number with no setup. The number is the first thing heard and the first thing seen.
Open with a direct question to the viewer, answered nowhere in the first ten seconds.
State something the viewer already believes as if agreeing, then break it on the next line.
Open mid-action, mid-sentence, as if the viewer has walked in on something already happening.
Open on one very specific physical detail — a sound, a posture, an object — and widen out from it.
Name the viewer and their situation in the first clause, so they know immediately it is about them.
Put two true statements side by side that cannot both be comfortable, and let the tension carry the first ten seconds.
Open on one named person at one moment in time, and stay with them until the problem is felt.
Three numbers in three seconds, each one landing on a hard cut, before a word of explanation.
Open on a sound the viewer recognises, with the picture arriving a beat late.
